newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors stymied as market up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors stymied as market up.

text.p: Investors in U.S. stock index options were somewhat stymied Tuesday as the underlying markets continued their unrelenting surge into record ground, traders said.
"No one's ever seen anything like this," said Jay Shartsis, head of options trading at R.F. Lafferty in New York.

"In analyzing the market or any market, you have to go by past statistics and past performance," he said. "Of course, looking at anything in the past brings you to the conclusion that this (rally) should have stopped a long time ago."
By 1200 CST/1800 GMT, the bellwether Dow industrial average. DJI was up 46 points at 6,890, just off a fresh session high of 6,894. The intraday high was a record.
In the broader market, the S&P 100 index .OEX, was up 7.39 at 769.16 and the S&P 500 .SPX rose 6.34 to 783.04.
March S&P 500 futures were ahead 7.60 points at 787.75 after setting a new intraday record high at 788.40.
Traders pegged fair value at around 4.20 points premium to cash, with buy programs at a 5.75-point premium and sell programs at a 3.10-point premium.
Options traders said activity was relatively sluggish as investors scrambled to make sense of the continued rally.
"It's very slow," one index options trader in Chicago said of the day's trading. "I think people aren't sure what to do. The market just continues to move up."
Jerry Hegarty, an analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said one reason volumes have been so light is that "the options are too expensive to buy and too explosive to sell."
He cited the fact that on Monday, an at-the-money call was selling for around $18.
On Tuesday, the most active call in the OEX was the February 780, which traded 4,495 contracts. It was up 2-3/8 at 10-1/2.
The options closest to the money were the 770s. The February 770 call had volume of about 2,050 and rose 3-1/8 to 15-1/2. The same strike put traded fewer than 300 contracts and lost 4-1/4 to 15-1/4.
The most active OEX put was the February 740, which traded about 4,740 contracts. It fell two to 6-1/4.
Volumes were also light in SPX options on the CBOE, where the most action was in the February 820 call, which traded about 3,175 contracts.
The call was trading up 11/16 at 2-5/8. It had open interest of 4,153 contracts through Monday.
The SPX March 775 put traded a little more than 3,000 contracts.
Shartsis said one indication the market was set for a sharp move higher emerged Monday when it did not pull back after last week's expiration.

"I have observed over the years that if it doesn't drop right after expiration, then you get another upside explosion, which is what you're looking at here," he said. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
